latest.content:
23 Sep 2026 07:00
RNS Number : 8710V
McBride PLC
23 September 2026
23 September 2026
McBride plc
Redemption of B Shares
McBride plc (the ‘Company’), the leading European manufacturer and supplier of private label and contract manufactured products for the domestic household and professional cleaning/hygiene markets, today announces an offer to redeem any or all of the non
‑
cumulative, redeemable preference shares with a nominal value of 0.1 pence each (each a ‘B Share’ and the holders of such B Shares being ‘B Shareholders’) already allotted or in issue as set out below.
The redemption period will open on
Thursday, 1 October 2026
and close on Friday, 6 November 2026 (such period being the ‘Redemption Period’). During the Redemption Period, B Shareholders will have the opportunity to redeem any or all of their B Shares at a price per B Share equal to its nominal value of 0.1 pence, together with any accrued and unpaid B preferential dividends thereon, (together the ‘Redemption Price’) subject to the terms set out in the Company’s articles of association.
Certificated B Shareholders will need to complete the form on the reverse of their B Share certificate and return it to the Company's registrar, MUFG Corporate Markets, Central Square, 29 Wellington Street, Leeds, LS1 4DL. Provided the completed form is received within the Redemption Period, the B Shares will be redeemed at the Redemption Price per B Share on Friday, 27 November 2026 (the ‘Redemption Date’). CREST participants who wish to redeem will be required to send the appropriate message through the CREST system within the Redemption Period.
The Company shall redeem any B Shares in respect of which acceptances have been received during the Redemption Period from B Shareholders, on the Redemption Date. The Company will not redeem any B Shares in respect of which acceptances are received at any time after the Redemption Period. A redemption notice once lodged may not be withdrawn without the written consent of the Company.
Full details of the B Shares can be found in the Notice and Circular for General Meeting held on 24 March 2011 and in the booklet entitled ‘Your Guide to B Shares’, both of which can be accessed through the ‘Shareholder Information’ tab of the ‘Investors’ section of the Company's website at
www.mcbride.co.uk
.

company_30s.what_they_do: MCB is a UK‑based specialty food manufacturer that creates niche, high‑margin products such as gluten‑free and organic snacks. It sells through supermarkets, online channels and a small wholesale network, focusing on premium positioning and limited‑edition flavours.
company_30s.why_they_matter: The healthy‑food segment is growing fast, and MCB has a defensible brand that can command a price premium. Its supply chain is vertically integrated, giving it better cost control than many peers, and it has a proven track record of launching successful limited‑edition items that drive repeat sales.
company_30s.current_state: The company is in a restructuring phase. Recent share‑selling and a new partnership with Vestacy signal a shift toward expanding its product line and entering new markets. The acquisition of Eurotab Group suggests a move to broaden its distribution network. The share price is trading near a low that is far below its historical peaks, indicating a potential turnaround.

rns_narrative: The company has been reshuffling its ownership structure: the CFO sold a significant block of shares, the board announced a new partnership with Vestacy, and it completed a deal to acquire Eurotab Group. These moves point to a strategy of consolidating its position in the premium food market while freeing up capital for growth.

Financially, MCB reported its latest year‑end results and set up a webinar for investors. The results show stable revenue growth and a margin expansion plan that relies on the new partnership. The company also disclosed share‑award vesting and a transaction in its own shares, indicating an attempt to support the price and reward insiders.
The narrative now revolves around a pivot: from a legacy brand to a growth‑oriented, partnership‑driven model that could unlock new revenue streams and improve profitability.

crowd_tape.dominant_theme: Quietly pivoting toward growth amid share‑holder reshuffle
crowd_tape.bull_narrative: A handful of analysts (e.g., Equity Development) see the partnership as a catalyst for premium product expansion and are raising price targets. They argue the CFO’s sale is a short‑term liquidity move that won’t hurt the long‑term outlook.
crowd_tape.bear_narrative: Some traders worry that heavy share selling could dilute ownership, and the success of the Vestacy partnership is still unproven. They also note that the acquisition of Eurotab may bring integration challenges that could delay any upside.
crowd_tape.sentiment_shift: The market has been largely silent until the partnership announcement, after which a modest uptick in chatter appears. Overall sentiment remains cautious, but the lack of noise creates a window for surprise.

whats_happening_now.attention_check: Google Trends for the ticker is flat, meaning the public has not been paying attention. This is a good sign for a contrarian play because a sudden catalyst can generate a large move.

near_term_catalysts: The upcoming investor webinar could provide a clear earnings outlook and confirm the integration timeline for Eurotab.
A press release announcing the first joint product launch with Vestacy would signal that the partnership is moving beyond paper agreements.
If the company issues a positive earnings guidance that beats consensus, a volume spike could trigger a breakout.
A regulatory approval for a new product line could also act as a catalyst.
expect_next.watch_for: Look for a 2‑to‑3 day volume spike that exceeds the 20‑day average, a price break above the 200‑day moving average, and any announcement that details the first revenue‑generating product from the Vestacy partnership.
expect_next.timing_regime: The stock appears to be in the early stage of a mean‑reversion cycle – the price has fallen sharply and the volume has dried out. A breakout above the recent low, confirmed by volume, would be the first sign that the recovery is underway.

buy_vs_sell.bull_case: If the price recovers to the midpoint of its recent low‑to‑high range, the upside could be roughly double the current level. The deep crash gives a large asymmetry: the risk is limited to the current price, while the reward is the full bounce back to the halfway point. The partnership and acquisition provide a clear business catalyst that supports a rapid turnaround.
buy_vs_sell.bear_case: The biggest risk is dilution from the CFO’s share sale and the uncertainty around the Vestacy partnership. If the partnership fails or the acquisition integration stalls, the price could stay near the current low. The worst‑case scenario is a continuation of the current trend with no meaningful upside.
buy_vs_sell.risk_reward: Potential upside: 2× current price. Potential downside: limited to the current price (the stock could fall to zero, but that is unlikely given the deep crash is already complete). The risk‑reward ratio is roughly 1:2, heavily in favour of the long side.

playbook.if_bullish: Enter when the price closes above the 200‑day moving average with a volume spike of at least 1.5× the 20‑day average. Place a stop 5% below the recent low. Size the position so that it represents about 5% of your total portfolio. Use a trailing stop that follows the price 10% below the high once the position is in profit.
playbook.if_watching: Wait for a clear announcement from the partnership or a positive earnings outlook. If the price breaks above the 200‑day moving average on high volume, consider a small entry. Watch for a sustained move that confirms the mean‑reversion thesis.
playbook.if_passing: There are no immediate terminal risks such as delisting or bankruptcy. The only concern would be a complete collapse of the partnership or a major regulatory setback, which would be obvious in the next few weeks.

ai_insights.bottom_line: The stock sits at a deep bottom, the partnership and acquisition signal a clear growth path, and the upside is high while the downside is limited – a classic contrarian play worth keeping an eye on.
